findings.claim: NewMonth.runCatchUp runs advanceDueDates first. That function stamps finishedAt = today as soon as the chain's next step passes endDate. After that, the month replay sweeps nothing for the months before endDate, and it never reaches the completion notice or the linked Loan's closing row. Both of those require finishedAt == null. Example: someone opens the app on 20 Oct after a final occurrence on 15 Oct. The expense is marked finished that day, so on 1 Nov there is no notice and no "Loan finished" row. After a multi-month absence, the real sweeps before endDate are silently skipped, which breaks §3.9's "never silently skipped".
findings.evidence: Recurring.kt:161 "if (e.endDate != null && nxt > e.endDate) { finishedAt = finishedAt ?: today; break }"; Recurring.kt:299 "if (e.finishedAt != null) return next to 0"; NewMonth.kt:70 "if (e.endDate != null && e.finishedAt == null && first >= e.endDate) {". The only endDate test (NewMonthTest.kt:74) starts with dueDate already past endDate, so it never reaches this path.
findings.proposed_fix: In advanceDueDates, stop the chain at endDate without setting finishedAt, and leave finishing to processMonth, or set finishedAt to the final occurrence date and let processMonth sweep months up to and including it. Add tests for (a) an open between the last occurrence and the next 1st, and (b) a 3-month absence that spans endDate. Both should assert the swept rows, the notice and the "Loan finished" row.

findings.claim: registrations() drops any reminder whose fire date is today or earlier, even though it is due at 09:00 and the sync may run earlier that day. Every sync clears the OS set and re-lays it: every app open, every write, and on Windows the 08:30 daily task. So a sync before 09:00 on the fire day cancels that day's reminder. The test assumes the app fires it instead, but Reminders.fireDue is never called in production code and nothing ever sets lastReminderFiredFor. On Windows the reminder is therefore lost almost every time; on Android it is lost whenever the app is opened before 09:00 on the fire day.
findings.evidence: Reminders.kt:74 "if (r.fireDate <= today || e.lastReminderFiredFor == e.dueDate) continue"; RemindersTest.kt:60 "// fire day reached: the app fires it, not the OS"; Windows task: "New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Daily -At 08:30". A grep for fireDue finds only its declaration and tests.
findings.proposed_fix: Filter on the instant rather than the day: keep a registration while fireAt is still in the future (both platforms already drop past instants). Either wire fireDue into the delivery path so lastReminderFiredFor is recorded, or delete it along with the field's dead guard. Add a test for a sync at 08:30 on the fire day.

findings.claim: Both setNewMonthNotification implementations cancel whatever is pending and re-arm starting from the 1st of next month. Both are called on every sync. A sync on the 1st before 09:00 therefore cancels that day's ping. On Windows the daily --sync-notifications task runs at 08:30 (with StartWhenAvailable), so the ping §3.9 says fires "on the 1st of every calendar month, unconditionally" never fires on a machine that is on at 08:30. On Android, opening the app or writing anything before 09:00 on the 1st has the same effect through REPLACE.
findings.evidence: windows.kt:146 removes every 'newmonth-*' toast, then :148 "var month = LocalDate(today.year, today.month, 1).plus(1, DateTimeUnit.MONTH)"; android.kt:203-204 "LocalDate(now.year, now.month, 1).plus(1, DateTimeUnit.MONTH)" with ExistingWorkPolicy.REPLACE
findings.proposed_fix: Start from this month's 1st at NOTIFY_HOUR when that instant is still in the future, otherwise next month's. On Android, use ExistingWorkPolicy.KEEP (or skip the enqueue when the pending work already targets the same instant). Add a unit test that computes the next fire instant from a clock at 08:30 on the 1st.

findings.claim: catchUpSummaryPending is persisted, but the card renders from the in-memory state.catchUp, which only the open that ran the catch-up fills in. If the process dies before the person dismisses the card, the next open replays nothing, catchUp is null, and the card never renders, even though the flag is still true. The flag can only be cleared from that card, so it stays true until another multi-month absence. Meanwhile §11.3's goal prompt, gated on !catchUpSummaryPending, never appears. The persisted catchUpDepositCount/Total look like the intended fix, but they are only ever incremented, never read or reset.
findings.evidence: BudgetScreen.kt:194 "val s = state.catchUp ?: return"; :235 "state.catchUp == null && !s.catchUpSummaryPending"; BudgetScreen.kt:187 KDoc claims "It persists until dismissed (`catchUpSummaryPending`)"; Income.kt:96 "catchUpDepositCount = cur.settings.catchUpDepositCount + count" (never read outside a test)
findings.proposed_fix: Persist the summary's figures (months replayed, swept total, deposits, ended notices) with the pending flag, rebuild the card from them when state.catchUp is null, and reset the accumulators on dismiss. Or, at minimum, clear the flag when there is no summary to show. Add a store test: run a catch-up, rebuild the store from the same DB, and assert that the card data is present.

findings.claim: Saving an Account links its chosen expense back to it, but it never clears the back-link on a previously linked expense, and it never clears linkedRecurringExpenseId when auto-update is turned off. After Account A is re-linked from expense X to expense Y, X still carries linkedAccountId = A. Deleting X then runs Recurring.delete's pair cascade, which removes Loan A and writes an "Account closed" row. The person only asked to delete an old payment.
findings.evidence: AccountEditing.kt:32-34 "cleaned.linkedRecurringExpenseId?.let { eid -> ... it.copy(linkedAccountId = cleaned.id) ..." (no un-link of the old id); Recurring.kt:277-280 "e.linkedAccountId?.let { accId -> ... next = next.copy(accounts = next.accounts.filter { it.id != accId })"
findings.proposed_fix: In AccountEditing.save, clear linkedAccountId on every expense that points at this account but is no longer its linkedRecurringExpenseId. Drop linkedRecurringExpenseId when autoUpdateFromPayments is cleaned to false (unless the link is a §9.2 pair). Add a test that re-links and then deletes the old expense, asserting that the account survives.

findings.claim: create() derives firstDueDate, dueDateAnchorDay, intervalDays and a normalised dueDate. edit() stores the draft as is. Edit a fixed-date expense from the 1st to the 15th and dueDateAnchorDay stays 1, so the sweep walk (which reads the anchor) keeps sweeping on the 1st, and the chain snaps dueDate back to the 1st on the next advance. Switching interval to fixed leaves the anchor null, so the walk uses firstDueDate.day while the chain uses the drifted dueDate.day. A past date typed in an edit is not normalised, which also skews the recomputed apportioned share. §3.11 treats a changed dueDate as "a new plan".
findings.evidence: Recurring.kt:224 "var e = edited.copy(profileId = d.profileId)" (no anchor or interval derivation); Recurring.kt:49 "else listOf(e.dueDateAnchorDay ?: floor.day)"; Recurring.kt:193 "dueDateAnchorDay = if (dateMode == DateMode.FIXED_DATE) draft.dueDate.day else null" (create only). No RecurringTest case edits dueDate or dateMode.
findings.proposed_fix: Factor create()'s derivation (dateMode nulling, anchor day, interval, normalisedNextDue) into one function and apply it in edit() whenever planChanged() is true. Add tests that edit the due day and the date mode, then assert the next month's sweep date and the advanced dueDate.

findings.claim: NewMonth.runCatchUp runs only in AppSession.open(), on the Profile active at launch. switchProfile loads the other Profile raw. If that Profile was last active months ago, its Category spent totals, sweeps, auto-deposits and dueDate chain stay stale for the rest of the session: Budget shows last month's spent and Savings is missing its sweeps until the app restarts. The previous Profile's catchUp summary also stays in UiState.
findings.evidence: AppStore.kt:468-471 "val d = dao.load(id) ?: return@withLock ... _state.update { it.copy(data = d, appState = dao.appState(), sheet = null) }"; AppSession.kt:34 "val (after, summary) = NewMonth.runCatchUp(loaded, clock, newId)" (open only)
findings.proposed_fix: Route switchProfile (and deleteProfile's fallback and reloadAll after restore) through one AppSession.activate(id) that runs runCatchUp, saves, syncs notifications and returns the summary. Replace state.catchUp with that summary. Add a SettingsStoreTest case that switches to a Profile last swept two months ago.

findings.claim: setCadence nulls incomePayDate, and incomePayDate2 starts null, but the Income page's date fields display today's date when the stored value is null. After a cadence change the person sees a payday that the engine does not have. nextOccurrence then returns null (no auto-deposits, no "no income logged" note). For semimonthly with a null second date, it falls back to one deposit a month.
findings.evidence: SettingsScreens.kt:238 "DateField(s.incomePayDate ?: store.clock.today()) { ... }"; :242 "DateField(s.incomePayDate2 ?: store.clock.today())"; Income.kt:150 "incomePayDate = null,"; Income.kt:34 "val anchor = s.incomePayDate ?: return null"

Decide which reading §3.3's "re-asks the anchor" wants, then add a test that auto-deposit is inert until the date is chosen.

findings.claim: The AppStore, AppSession and Room database are built in onCreate and held only by the Activity. There is no ViewModel and no configChanges. Every rotation, dark-mode flip, font-scale or locale change rebuilds them and calls start() again. The route stack, open sheet, import review, pending backup and editor drafts are all lost. The app returns to Budget, catch-up and notification sync run again, and a second database instance is opened each time. The AppStore KDoc says transient state "must survive a recomposition but never a restart", but a rotation is neither.
findings.evidence: MainActivity.kt:78-81 "val db = buildSciFinDatabase(applicationContext) ... val store = AppStore(session, db, lifecycleScope, files) ... lifecycleScope.launch { store.start() }"; manifest <activity> has no android:configChanges
findings.proposed_fix: Hold the database, session and store in an Application-scoped singleton or a ViewModel (with the store's scope = viewModelScope), and keep only the launchers and the Files bridge in the Activity. Guard start() so it runs once per process.

findings.claim: At a tab root the Back callback disables itself and forwards to the system. Since Android 12, Back on a root launcher activity moves the task to the background instead of finishing the activity. The same instance comes back with the callback still disabled, so from then on Back leaves the app from any pushed screen or editor instead of popping the route stack.
findings.evidence: MainActivity.kt:82 "onBackPressedDispatcher.addCallback(this) { if (!store.back()) { isEnabled = false; onBackPressedDispatcher.onBackPressed() } }"
findings.proposed_fix: Drive isEnabled from state (enabled while routes.size > 1 or a sheet is open), collecting store.state in lifecycleScope, and never flip it off inside the handler. Or re-enable it in onResume.

findings.claim: §4.7's restore is "replace, not merge", but Backup.apply is a sequence of separate transactions: one save per Profile, then one delete per surplus Profile, then the app-state row. A failure or process death partway through leaves a device holding some restored Profiles, some old ones, and an activeProfileId that may point at either. That is a merge the person never agreed to, with no rollback. The pre-open Snapshot only covers schema migrations.
findings.evidence: Backup.kt:147-150 "for (p in b.profiles) dao.save(p)" then "for (id in existing) if (...) dao.deleteProfileWhole(id)" then "dao.upsertAppState(AppState(activeProfileId = b.activeProfileId, ..."
findings.proposed_fix: Make it one @Transaction DAO method, restoreAll(profiles, activeId, dates), that deletes every Profile's rows and writes the backup's inside a single transaction (or wrap the calls in db.useWriterConnection { it.immediateTransaction { ... } }). Add a test that throws midway and asserts the pre-restore state.

findings.claim: No store path catches an exception. pickStatement, pickBackup, exportBackup and dispatch all launch in the host scope. That is Android's lifecycleScope, which has no CoroutineExceptionHandler. The SAF bridge calls contentResolver open/read/write unguarded. So a revoked or unreadable URI, a cloud provider that fails to write, a non-UTF-8 or huge file, or a disk-full Room write crashes the process mid-action. The UI has backupError/importError lines ready to say what went wrong, but nothing sets them on these failures.
findings.evidence: MainActivity.kt:57 "contentResolver.openInputStream(uri)?.use { it.readBytes().toString(Charsets.UTF_8) }"; :64 "contentResolver.openOutputStream(uri)?.use { it.write(text.toByteArray(Charsets.UTF_8)) }"; AppStore.kt:380 "val picked = files.open(listOf(\"csv\", \"ofx\", \"qfx\", \"txt\")) ?: return@launch"
findings.proposed_fix: Catch IOException and SecurityException in the Files implementations (returning null/false). In AppStore, wrap the file and DB work in runCatching and route failures to importError/backupError, plus a generic save-failed line for dispatch. Give the Android scope a CoroutineExceptionHandler as a backstop.

findings.claim: Headers are matched by substring and "value" is an amount keyword. A common bank header such as "Booking date,Value date,Description,Amount" therefore resolves the amount column to "Value date", since it is the first header containing "value". Every amount then parses to null and every row is dropped, and the person is told the file has no amount column. The same substring rule lets "credit" match headers like "Credit card number".
findings.evidence: Import.kt:99 "private val AMOUNT_KEYS = listOf(\"amount\", \"importo\", \"betrag\", \"value\", ..."; Import.kt:97 DATE_KEYS includes "value date"; Import.kt:124 "fun find(keys: List<String>) = header.indexOfFirst { h -> keys.any { h.contains(it) } }"
findings.proposed_fix: Prefer exact header matches over substring matches, exclude columns already claimed by the date matcher, and rank keywords ("amount" before "value"). Add ImportBackupTest cases for a Booking date/Value date/Amount header and a Credit card number column.

findings.claim: Each import-review row's include toggle is a bare 19dp box with .clickable. It has no Role.Checkbox, no toggleable state and no label, so TalkBack or Narrator announces an unlabelled clickable with no checked state. Its hit area is also far below §2.5's 48dp/40dp target floor. CheckboxRow in Progress.kt already does this correctly with toggleable(role = Role.Checkbox) at target height, but it was re-drawn by hand here instead of reused. The .let at line 87 that adds a transparent background to excluded rows is a no-op.
findings.evidence: ImportScreen.kt:92-93 "Modifier.size(19.dp).background(...).border(...)" then ".clickable { store.toggleImportRow(i) }"; Progress.kt:132 "toggleable(value = checked, role = Role.Checkbox)"; ImportScreen.kt:87 "it.background(p.bg.copy(alpha = 0f))"
findings.proposed_fix: Make the whole row (or at least a target-sized box) toggleable(value = r.include, role = Role.Checkbox) with the description as its label, sharing a Checkbox mark composable with CheckboxRow. Delete the no-op alpha-0 background.

findings.claim: Tokens defines screen-scaled IconSizes (xs/sm/md/lg), and §2.5 says the phone factor multiplies "icon and glyph sizes". No code reads t.icons: there are 0 references to icons.xs/sm/md/lg. The defaults are literals (LucideIcon 20.dp, EntityIcon 16.dp), and 32 call sites pass literal sizes, including the 13dp and 17dp values the IconSizes KDoc says were rationalised away. Icons therefore do not scale on 320dp or 480dp phones.
findings.evidence: Tokens.kt:113-115 "Four steps, rationalised from the six the build had grown (12 / 13 / 14 / 16 / 17 / 20)"; Icons.kt:86 "size: Dp = 20.dp"; Rows.kt:76 "LucideIcon(icon, tint = p.txt2, size = 17.dp)"; ReportsScreen.kt:162 "size = 13.dp"
findings.proposed_fix: Default LucideIcon/EntityIcon to LocalTokens.current.icons.* and replace the 32 literals with the nearest of the four steps. Add a speccheck/selftest rule that fails on `size = <n>.dp` in commonMain/ui.

findings.claim: The editor's trash button (border, target height, Role.Button, contentDescription "Delete", 16dp icon) is pasted into four editors. Each copy repeats an unscaled `padding(horizontal = 16.dp)`, which breaks the rule that every spacing value is a multiple of the scaled `gap`. The generic "Delete" label also never names what is being deleted.

findings.proposed_fix: Extract an EditorDeleteButton(label: String, onClick) into components, with padding in t.spacing units and a content description such as "Delete <name>". Use it in all four editors.

findings.claim: There are two money formatters and two month tables that disagree. The notification body shows exact cents and day-month order ("€950 · due 30 Sep"), while every screen rounds to whole units and puts the month first ("Sep 30"). The engine's formatter knows GBP and falls back to "<code> "; the UI's falls back to "€". Format.kt's claim to be the only formatter is false.
findings.evidence: Format.kt:8 "The display layer's formatting -- the only place minor units become text (§12)"; Reminders.kt:93 "fun formatMoney(amount: Money, currency: String): String {" with "\"GBP\" -> \"£\""; Reminders.kt:107 "fun formatDayMonth(d: LocalDate): String = \"${d.day} ${MONTHS[d.monthNumber - 1]}\""
findings.proposed_fix: Pick one date order and one rounding rule for notification text versus screens. Then move a single formatter (money + date + month names + currency table) into a common non-UI package that both Reminders and ui/Format use, and delete the duplicate.

findings.claim: Settings offers USD, but some text is pinned to euros whatever the Profile's currency is. The Age of Money note says "the oldest euro". The tutorial's mock Savings row always shows "€1,240". currencySymbol silently falls back to € for any code it does not know.
findings.evidence: ReportsScreen.kt:174 "it counts from today back to the oldest euro still sitting in Savings"; Tutorial.kt:20 "mock = \"Savings — €1,240\""; Format.kt:16 "fun currencySymbol(code: String): String = CURRENCY_SYMBOLS[code] ?: \"€\""
findings.proposed_fix: Say "the oldest money" (or format with the Profile's currency), build the tutorial mock through formatMoney(124000, currency), and make currencySymbol fall back to the code itself rather than another currency's symbol.

findings.claim: Several KDocs contradict the code beside them. The database class still states a pre-v1 destructive-migration policy, while finishBuilding says every shipped version has a migration path. The replay page says the replay button is still to come, yet it is on the page, and that the tour has eight stops "until §8 ships", yet TUTORIAL_STOPS has nine and §8 has shipped. Radii/Strokes are documented as scaling on the screen axis, but the next data class says they are fixed on every axis.
findings.evidence: SciFinDatabase.kt:34 "Pre-v1 policy (§12): destructive migration." vs :61 "every shipped version has a path"; SettingsScreens.kt:328 "the replay button arrives with the tutorial" (button at :351); :333 "the tour itself has eight stops until §8 ships"; Tokens.kt:68 "the screen axis only" vs :77 "Fixed dp on every axis"
findings.proposed_fix: Rewrite the four comments to match current behaviour: migrations plus a destructive fallback under the pre-open snapshot, nine stops with the replay button present, and radii/strokes fixed dp.

findings.claim: Any sync that runs on a notification's fire day before 09:00 cancels that day's notification. registrations() filters by date, not time, so a reminder due today at 09:00 is left out, and the declarative sync cancels whatever is left out. setNewMonthNotification always starts from next month's 1st. On Windows the daily top-up task runs at 08:30 and calls both, so with the machine on it removes every due-date reminder, import reminder and New Month toast about 30 minutes before it would fire. On Android, opening the app or saving anything before 09:00 does the same. The test pins this behaviour with a false comment: nothing in production fires the reminder in-app.
findings.evidence: Reminders.kt:74 "if (r.fireDate <= today || e.lastReminderFiredFor == e.dueDate) continue"; Reminders.kt:83 "nextImportReminder(d, today.plusDays(1))"; windows.kt:148 "var month = LocalDate(today.year, today.month, 1).plus(1, DateTimeUnit.MONTH)"; windows.kt:246 "-Trigger (New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Daily -At 08:30)"; android.kt:203-204 "LocalDate(now.year, now.month, 1).plus(1, DateTimeUnit.MONTH)"; RemindersTest.kt:60 "// fire day reached: the app fires it, not the OS"; §3.9 "fires on the 1st of every calendar month, unconditionally"
findings.proposed_fix: Filter on the instant, not the date: keep a registration while fireAt is still after now, and let the schedulers' own delayMs<=0 / fireAt<=now checks drop past ones. Start the New Month series at this month's 1st at NOTIFY_HOUR when that time is still ahead. Rewrite RemindersTest:60 to assert the fire-day registration survives a sync made before 09:00, and add a matching test for the New Month start month.

findings.claim: The catch-up card only renders while the in-memory CatchUpSummary exists, and that summary exists only on the open that ran the catch-up. On any later open in the same month, runCatchUp takes the early branch and returns null, so the card disappears while catchUpSummaryPending stays true. This is exactly the failure the flag was added to prevent. The card can then never be shown or dismissed, and because GoalPrompt requires !catchUpSummaryPending, §11.3's goal prompt is also blocked until another multi-month absence happens. An Android rotation re-runs start() and hides the card the same way.
findings.evidence: NewMonth.kt:123-125 "if (marks.isEmpty() || marks.first() >= nowYm) { ... return afterIncome to null"; BudgetScreen.kt:194 "val s = state.catchUp ?: return"; BudgetScreen.kt:235 "state.catchUp == null && !s.catchUpSummaryPending"; §3.9 "Without a flag it could only render on the open that ran the catch-up"
findings.proposed_fix: Persist what the card shows: months replayed, the swept total and the ended notices, next to the deposit counters that already exist. Build the card from the stored values whenever catchUpSummaryPending is true, and clear the stored values in dismissCatchUpCard. Add a store test: run a catch-up, restart the AppStore on the same database, and assert the card data is still there.

findings.claim: When the app goes unopened, reminders after the first one never fire. On Windows, restoreAfterBoot (the daily and logon top-up) builds registrations from the stored dueDates without running Recurring.advanceDueDates, so once an occurrence passes, every later one is filtered out as past. On Android there is no top-up at all: a fired NotifyWorker is never followed by the next occurrence, and the monthly import reminder is a one-shot that never re-arms. The spec says a missed import reminder is followed by next month's 'as scheduled'.
findings.evidence: AppSession.kt:70-71 "val d = dao.load(app.activeProfileId) ?: return / scheduler.restoreAfterBoot(Reminders.registrations(d, clock.today()), ..."; §3.11 "a build that ran the chain only from the month-boundary path left every dueDate stale"; §3.11 "a reminder that only appears once you have already opened the app is not a reminder"; §11.5 "The next month's fires as scheduled."
findings.proposed_fix: In restoreAfterBoot, compute registrations from Recurring.advanceDueDates(d, today), in memory with no money moved and no save, and fall back to the first Profile as open() does. On Android, add a daily periodic Worker that runs the same restore, or have NotifyWorker enqueue the next occurrence. Add a test that restoreAfterBoot two months after the last open still registers the next reminder.

findings.claim: On Android 13 and later, a denied or revoked POST_NOTIFICATIONS permission is reported as NOT_ASKED, and §4.7's line only renders for DENIED. So the case the line exists for (the toggle shows on while nothing can fire) never shows it on current Android. The permission is also read only in start(), never on resume. The stored notificationPermissionGranted field is written but never read, although §4.7 names it as the one field this surface reads.
findings.evidence: android.kt:90 "if (!granted) return NotificationPermission.NOT_ASKED"; SettingsScreens.kt:261 "if (state.notificationPermission == NotificationPermission.DENIED) FeasibilityNote("; §4.7 "a toggle that displays as on while nothing can ever fire is the app misreporting its own state"
findings.proposed_fix: Return NOT_ASKED only while the stored notificationPermissionGranted is null, meaning it was never asked; otherwise return DENIED when the permission is not granted. Alternatively, show the Settings line for any value other than GRANTED once onboarding is complete. Re-read the permission when the activity resumes (ON_RESUME), not only in onCreate.

findings.claim: The AppStore, the Room database and the picker deferreds are created in onCreate, with no ViewModel and no configChanges. Rotation, a system dark-mode switch or a locale change recreates the activity. That resets routes to Budget, drops an open sheet, an import review or a validated backup awaiting Confirm, re-runs session.open(), and builds a second Room instance while the first is never closed. If the activity is recreated while the SAF picker is up, the result reaches a new pendingOpen that is null, so the chosen file is silently ignored.
findings.evidence: MainActivity.kt:78-81 "val db = buildSciFinDatabase(applicationContext) ... val store = AppStore(session, db, lifecycleScope, files) / lifecycleScope.launch { store.start() }"; MainActivity.kt:49 "registerForActivityResult(ActivityResultContracts.OpenDocument()) { uri -> pendingOpen?.complete(uri); pendingOpen = null }"
findings.proposed_fix: Hold the database, session and AppStore in a ViewModel (or an Application-scoped singleton) with viewModelScope, so the store survives recreation. Keep only the launchers in the Activity. Have the store own the pending-pick continuation so a recreated Activity can complete it.

findings.claim: NewMonth.runCatchUp runs only in AppSession.open(). Switching to a Profile that has been dormant since an earlier month, or restoring a backup (reloadAll), shows last month's un-reset spent, unswept expenses, stale dueDates and missed auto-deposits until the app is restarted. On Android and desktop a long-lived process never re-runs it across the 1st. Separately, syncReminders cancels the whole reminder set and registers only the active Profile's, so every other Profile's due-date and import reminders are silently cancelled on switch.
findings.evidence: AppStore.kt:468 "val d = dao.load(id) ?: return@withLock" (no catch-up); AppSession.kt:33 "val (after, summary) = NewMonth.runCatchUp(loaded, clock, newId)" (only call site); android.kt:122 "work.cancelAllWorkByTag(TAG_REMINDER)"; §8.4 "A Profile is a genuinely separate environment"
findings.proposed_fix: Route switchProfile and reloadAll through one AppSession.activate(id) that runs runCatchUp, saves and syncs, and re-run it on resume when the month has changed. Decide whether reminders are per-device (the union over all Profiles, keyed by profileId plus expenseId) or active-Profile only, and state the decision in §3.11 and §8.4.

findings.claim: Backup.apply's doc comment says the store is replaced whole in one transaction, but apply is a plain function. Each dao.save and deleteProfileWhole is its own @Transaction, and the AppState upsert is separate again. A failure or process death part way through leaves some profiles replaced, others not yet deleted, and a stale activeProfileId, which is a half-merged store the replace-not-merge rule forbids. No exception is caught, so on Android the failure also crashes the app.
findings.evidence: Backup.kt:143 "/** Write everything first, then load: the store is replaced whole, in one transaction. */"; Backup.kt:147-148 "for (p in b.profiles) dao.save(p) / for (id in existing) if (...) dao.deleteProfileWhole(id)"
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap the whole body in a single transaction: a @Transaction DAO method replaceAll(profiles, appState), or db.useWriterConnection { it.immediateTransaction { ... } }. Catch failures in confirmBackup and surface them as backupError. Add a test that injects a failure on the second profile and asserts the store is unchanged.

findings.claim: Every file boundary lets exceptions escape. A revoked URI, SecurityException, FileNotFoundException, unreadable file or full disk in open/save propagates out of pickStatement, pickBackup or exportBackup, which have no try/catch. On Android that crashes the app through lifecycleScope. On desktop the SupervisorJob scope has no handler, so the exception goes to the thread's uncaught-exception handler (usually a stack trace on stderr, invisible in the console-less packaged app) and the person sees nothing: no refusal, no retry.
findings.evidence: MainActivity.kt:57 "val text = contentResolver.openInputStream(uri)?.use { it.readBytes().toString(Charsets.UTF_8) } ?: return null"; MainActivity.kt:64 "contentResolver.openOutputStream(uri)?.use { it.write(text.toByteArray(Charsets.UTF_8)) } ?: return false"; AppStore.kt:436 "val picked = files.open(listOf("json")) ?: return@launch"
findings.proposed_fix: Catch IOException and SecurityException inside both Files implementations and return a typed failure. Map it to importError, backupError or an export-failed line in the store. Add a CoroutineExceptionHandler to the desktop scope that logs to launch.log.

findings.claim: Two public top-level formatMoney functions disagree. The engine version, used for notification bodies, knows GBP and prints other codes verbatim with exact cents. The UI version knows only EUR and USD, silently shows '€' for any other code, and rounds to whole units. Backup.validate repairs only theme and mode, so a restored or future currency such as GBP or CHF shows € throughout the app while its reminders say £ or CHF. That is a displayed fact that is wrong.
findings.evidence: Reminders.kt:94 "val symbol = when (currency) { "EUR" -> "€"; "USD" -> "$"; "GBP" -> "£"; else -> "$currency " }"; Format.kt:16 "fun currencySymbol(code: String): String = CURRENCY_SYMBOLS[code] ?: "€""; RemindersTest.kt:78 "assertEquals("CHF 9.99", formatMoney(moneyOf(9.99), "CHF"))"
findings.proposed_fix: Keep one currency table and one symbol function in commonMain, used by both the engine and the UI (the engine keeping exact cents is fine). Decide whether unknown currencies are refused or repaired at restore in Backup.validate, and never map an unknown code to €.

findings.claim: Every dispatch on Windows runs session.syncNotifications while holding the writes mutex, and that spawns two synchronous PowerShell processes, each allowed a 20 s timeout, re-registering twelve New Month toasts even when nothing notification-related changed. The Income field dispatches on every keystroke, so typing '1500' queues about eight PowerShell runs behind the mutex. The desktop launch also runs several PowerShell calls under runBlocking before the window opens: permissionState, the syncs, and installIfNeeded's check.
findings.evidence: AppStore.kt:267-268 "db.dao().save(after) / session.syncNotifications(after)"; SettingsScreens.kt:230 "TextField(amountText, { v -> amountText = v; parseMoney(v)?.let { m -> store.updateSettings { it.copy(income = m) } }"; windows.kt:317 "p.waitFor(20, TimeUnit.SECONDS)"
findings.proposed_fix: Sync only when the registration list or the New Month flag actually changed: compare against the last value handed to the scheduler. Run the sync off the writes mutex, debounced. Commit text-field money edits on blur or on Done rather than on every keystroke.

findings.claim: catchUpDepositCount and catchUpDepositTotal are added to on every auto-deposit, never reset (not even on dismiss) and never read, so they grow without bound in every Profile and every backup. notificationPermissionGranted is written at onboarding and never read. All three are schema columns and backup fields that carry no behaviour.
findings.evidence: Income.kt:96-97 "catchUpDepositCount = cur.settings.catchUpDepositCount + count, / catchUpDepositTotal = cur.settings.catchUpDepositTotal + total,"; grep shows no reader outside Income.kt and Entities.kt; AppStore.kt:158 "notificationPermissionGranted = answer == NotificationPermission.GRANTED" (only reference)
findings.proposed_fix: Either give the counters their job (the persisted card in catchup-card-not-persistent, reset on dismiss) or delete them through a schema migration. Make notificationPermissionGranted the 'was asked' signal for android-denied-reads-not-asked, or remove it.

findings.claim: Reminders.fireDue is called only from tests, so lastReminderFiredFor is never set in production. Recurring.kt only ever resets it to null. Both schedulers and the seam's KDoc say this field is what stops a reboot re-firing a reminder, but that guard is really the date filter alone, which is the source of fire-day-reminders-cancelled.
findings.evidence: android.kt:130 "firing it here is exactly the reboot-re-fires-what-already-fired bug §12's lastReminderFiredFor exists to stop"; grep: fireDue referenced only in RemindersTest.kt:41-48; Recurring.kt:195 "lastReminderFiredFor = null"
findings.proposed_fix: Either delete fireDue and correct the three comments to name the real guard (fireAt <= now), or wire it up: have the delivering worker or toast record the fired due date. That needs a DB write from the worker, so it is a design choice. Remove the field in a migration if it stays unused.

findings.claim: §4.8 rule 2 (list-detail at 840dp) was withdrawn on 2026-09-24, but its scaffolding is still there. UiState.twoPane has no reader. WidthClass.EXPANDED is distinguished from MEDIUM only by a test, since the one consumer checks != COMPACT. Frame's TabScreen is documented as 'for the left pane' and wraps a one-branch `when (r) { else -> ... }`. Route.kt still cites the pane rule as a reason for the design.
findings.evidence: AppStore.kt:78-79 "§4.8 rule 2: list-detail at 840dp and above ... val twoPane: Boolean get() = tab != Tab.REPORTS && !inOnboardingPage"; Frame.kt:116 "§4.8's rule 2 was withdrawn 2026\-09\-24"; SheetHost.kt:37 "val wide = LocalWidthClass.current != WidthClass.COMPACT"
findings.proposed_fix: Delete twoPane. Collapse WidthClass to COMPACT/WIDE unless something is about to read EXPANDED, and update FrameRenderTest:124 to match. Simplify TabScreen and fix its KDoc and Route.kt's comment.

findings.claim: installAppRegistration's KDoc says the shortcut is rewritten to point at this executable each time, but installIfNeeded returns early whenever the daily task exists. After a reinstall to a different path, the AUMID shortcut and both scheduled tasks keep pointing at the old exe, so the top-up silently stops.
findings.evidence: windows.kt:174 "Idempotent: the shortcut is rewritten to point at this executable each time."; windows.kt:222 "if (schedulerEntriesInstalled()) return"
findings.proposed_fix: Compare the registered task's Execute path with executablePath and reinstall both the shortcut and the tasks when they differ, or always re-register (both are idempotent with -Force). Correct the KDoc.

findings.claim: Every other no-op path in AppStore returns a completed Job, but confirmImport returns `Job()`, which is active and never completes. A caller that joins it, as tests do on the happy path, hangs forever when no review is pending.
findings.evidence: AppStore.kt:398 "val review = _state.value.importReview ?: return Job()"; compare AppStore.kt:166 "?: return Job().apply { complete() }"
findings.proposed_fix: Return `Job().apply { complete() }`, or a shared `DONE` constant, as the other paths do.

verdicts.reason: Recurring.kt:161 `if (e.endDate != null && nxt > e.endDate) { finishedAt = finishedAt ?: today; break }` runs from NewMonth.runCatchUp:114 before any processMonth. sweepOccurrences (Recurring.kt:299) returns 0 once finishedAt != null for non-apportioned expenses. processMonth's completion branch (NewMonth.kt:70) and its Loan closing row both need finishedAt == null, and the auto-update loop skips when finishedAt != first. So an open between the last occurrence and the next 1st, or an absence that spans endDate, loses the notice, the 'Loan finished' row and any unswept pre-endDate months.

Reminders.kt:74 filters `r.fireDate <= today`, so a 09:00 reminder due today is left out. syncReminders cancels the whole tag first (android.kt:122; windows.kt:110). Every dispatch runs syncNotifications (AppStore.kt:267-268), and the Windows daily task runs at 08:30 (windows.kt:246). fireDue is referenced only in RemindersTest.kt:41-48, and nothing in production writes lastReminderFiredFor, so the comment at RemindersTest.kt:60 ('the app fires it') is false.

windows.kt:146-148 removes every newmonth-* toast, then starts at `LocalDate(today.year, today.month, 1).plus(1, DateTimeUnit.MONTH)`. android.kt:203-214 computes next month's 1st and enqueues it with ExistingWorkPolicy.REPLACE. Both run on every sync (AppSession.kt:61-64). A sync on the 1st before 09:00, such as the 08:30 task or any open or write, therefore replaces that day's ping, which contradicts §3.9 line 473 'fires on the 1st of every calendar month, unconditionally'.

BudgetScreen.kt:194 `val s = state.catchUp ?: return`, and state.catchUp is filled only from AppSession.open's summary. A later open takes runCatchUp's early branch (NewMonth.kt:118-120), which returns a null summary while catchUpSummaryPending stays true. The flag is cleared only by dismissCatchUpCard (AppStore.kt:338-340), which is reachable only from the unrendered card. GoalPrompt (BudgetScreen.kt:235) requires !catchUpSummaryPending, so the prompt stays blocked. catchUpDepositCount/Total are only incremented (Income.kt:96-97) and never read. This defeats §3.9 line 468.

AccountEditing.kt:32-34 sets linkedAccountId on the newly chosen expense only and never clears it on the old one. The editor lets the person re-pick the link (ActivityScreens.kt:300-301). Recurring.delete (Recurring.kt:277-281) then removes the account and logs 'Account closed' for any expense that still carries linkedAccountId.

Recurring.edit (Recurring.kt:220-230) stores the draft with only profileId and apportionedShare adjusted. The editor changes only dueDate and dateMode (RecurringEditorScreen.kt:107-113). dueDateAnchorDay, firstDueDate and intervalDays are derived only in create (Recurring.kt:189-195), and the sweep reads `e.dueDateAnchorDay ?: floor.day` (Recurring.kt:49). §3.11 line 507 says the anchor 'never changes on its own', and line 517 says an edit of dueDate 'is a new plan'.

The only runCatchUp call site is AppSession.kt:33. switchProfile (AppStore.kt:464-473) and reloadAll (AppStore.kt:127-133) load raw data and sync without a catch-up, and state.catchUp is not cleared on a switch.

SettingsScreens.kt:238 and :242 show `s.incomePayDate ?: store.clock.today()` and `s.incomePayDate2 ?: store.clock.today()`. Income.setCadence nulls incomePayDate (Income.kt:150). nextOccurrence returns null without an anchor (Income.kt:34), and semimonthly with no second date falls back to monthlyNext. DateField(value: LocalDate?, placeholder) already supports a null value (DateField.kt:41).

MainActivity.kt:78-81 builds the db, session and AppStore(lifecycleScope) inside onCreate and calls store.start(). There is no ViewModel, and the manifest's <activity> (AndroidManifest.xml:43) has no configChanges. Recreation rebuilds everything and re-runs session.open().

MainActivity.kt:82 `if (!store.back()) { isEnabled = false; onBackPressedDispatcher.onBackPressed() }`. Nothing re-enables the callback. On Android 12+ the fallback Back on a root launcher activity moves the task to the background instead of finishing it, so the same instance returns with the callback still disabled.

Backup.kt:144-151 runs separate calls: dao.save per profile, deleteProfileWhole per surplus profile, then upsertAppState. There is no enclosing transaction, although the KDoc at :143 says 'in one transaction'. confirmBackup (AppStore.kt:446-458) catches nothing.

verdicts.already_registered: §13.1 item 8 covers only the database open ('nothing catches the open'), not the file-picker or write paths
verdicts.reason: MainActivity.kt:57 and :64 call contentResolver open/read/write unguarded. AwtFiles.kt:21 and :30 call readText/writeText unguarded. pickStatement (AppStore.kt:378), pickBackup (:436) and exportBackup (:420) have no try/catch and run in lifecycleScope, which has no handler.

Import.kt:124 matches headers by substring, and AMOUNT_KEYS (Import.kt:99) includes 'value', so 'value date' wins at index 1. The consequence is worse than stated, though. amount() (Import.kt:40-46) keeps digits and '-', so '2026-09-01' becomes 20260901 minor units: the rows import as huge garbage amounts instead of being dropped. The 'credit' substring overreach is also real.

verdicts.already_registered: §13.3 'The scale and dark pass': '95 `N.dp` literals remain under shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/app/scifin/ui/' (general; does not name the unused IconSizes token)

verdicts.already_registered: §13.3: '`AppStore.kt:79`'s `twoPane` is dead code' (twoPane only; the rest unregistered)
verdicts.reason: A grep finds only the declarations of TabScreen (Frame.kt:130), twoPane (AppStore.kt:79), dismissCatchUp (AppStore.kt:274), parseIsoDate (Format.kt:86), monthAnchored (Enums.kt:17) and REMINDER_LEAD_DAYS (Enums.kt:85). verdicts.reason: ReportsScreen.kt:174 'back to the oldest euro still sitting in Savings'; Tutorial.kt:20 `mock = "Savings — €1,240"`; Format.kt:16 `CURRENCY_SYMBOLS[code] ?: "€"`. USD is offered (Format.kt:13), so a USD Profile sees euro text. The copy change is visible to the person.

SciFinDatabase.kt:34 'Pre-v1 policy (§12): destructive migration' vs :61 'every shipped version has a path'. SettingsScreens.kt:328 'the replay button arrives with the tutorial', while the button is present at :351. :333 'eight stops until §8 ships', while the list has nine and Tutorial.kt defines nine stops. Duplicate of code-A:fire-day-reminder-cancelled plus code-A:new-month-ping. Reminders.kt:74 and :83 (the import reminder also starts from today+1), windows.kt:148 and :246 (08:30 daily task), android.kt:203-214 REPLACE, RemindersTest.kt:60 false comment. All reproduced. The fix restores behaviour §3.9 and §3.11 already specify, so no decision is needed.

Duplicate of code-A:catch-up-card-lost. NewMonth.kt:118-120 returns `afterIncome to null` on later opens; BudgetScreen.kt:194 and :235 as quoted; spec line 468 'Without a flag it could only render on the open that ran the catch-up'. The behaviour is already decided by §3.9, so the fix is mechanical.

AppSession.restoreAfterBoot (AppSession.kt:67-72) builds registrations from stored dueDates without Recurring.advanceDueDates and does not fall back to the first Profile. That is the Windows 08:30 and logon path (Main.kt:47-48). On Android, NotifyWorker (android.kt:218-227) only posts, nothing enqueues the next occurrence or re-arms the import reminder, and there is no periodic worker. Spec §11.5 line 1177 says 'The next month's fires as scheduled.'

android.kt:89-90 returns NOT_ASKED whenever POST_NOTIFICATIONS is not granted on API 33+, including after a denial. SettingsScreens.kt:261 shows the line only for DENIED. The permission is read in start() (AppStore.kt:118) and nowhere on resume. notificationPermissionGranted is written at AppStore.kt:158 and never read.

Duplicate of code-A:android-activity-recreation-resets-store. Also MainActivity.kt:49: the launcher callback completes the new instance's pendingOpen, which is null after recreation, while the old coroutine is cancelled with the old lifecycleScope.

Catch-up half: as in code-A:switch-profile-skips-catch-up (AppStore.kt:468; AppSession.kt:33 is the only call site). Reminder half: syncReminders cancels the whole tag (android.kt:122) and is fed only the active Profile's registrations (AppSession.kt:62), so other Profiles' reminders are dropped on a switch. Duplicate of code-A:restore-not-atomic. The KDoc at Backup.kt:143 says 'in one transaction', but the body at :146-150 is separate DAO calls. confirmBackup (AppStore.kt:446-458) has no catch.

verdicts.reason: Duplicate of code-A:io-failures-crash-store. AwtFiles.kt:21 readText and :30 writeText are unguarded. The desktop scope is `CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob() + Dispatchers.Default)` (Main.kt:52) with no handler.

The two formatters are real (Reminders.kt:94 vs Format.kt:16), and the table disagreement is real. The 'wrong displayed fact' needs a currency outside EUR/USD, which Settings cannot set. It arises only through a hand-edited or future backup, since Backup.validate repairs only theme and mode. So the harm is conditional.

dispatch holds `writes` and calls session.syncNotifications (AppStore.kt:261-270). That runs syncReminders and setNewMonthNotification, each a powershell() call with a 20 s wait (windows.kt:317), and the latter re-registers 12 toasts. The Income TextField calls updateSettings on every parsed keystroke (SettingsScreens.kt:230). Committing on blur changes interaction slightly, but no user-facing decision is required.

findings.claim: Age of Money drops the excess when an outflow exceeds every remaining lot, when §5.1 says to carry it as a deficit. It also never floors at 0 when Savings is ≤ 0. After an overshoot, the next deposit opens a full datable lot, so the Buffer shows a positive age while Savings is negative, and the lot pool drifts permanently away from Savings.amount. No test covers a deficit.
findings.evidence: Spec §5.1 (line 785): "the excess is carried as a deficit that the next deposit absorbs before that deposit becomes a datable lot — it is not dropped" and "The figure floors at 0 when Savings ≤ 0". Code Reports.kt:39-47: `var toConsume = -effect` ... `if (toConsume <= 0) break` (leftover toConsume is discarded); Reports.kt:49-50 returns `oldest.first.daysTo(asOf)` with no check on savingsAmount. BufferReport (ReportsScreen.kt:143) guards only `d.savings.amount == null`.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep a running deficit in ageOfMoney. A positive effect first pays down the deficit and only the remainder opens a lot. Return 0 when the replayed balance (or d.savingsAmount for the live point) is ≤ 0. Add §5.1's worked test: €250 overshoot, then €1,000 deposit, then €400 sweep leaves lots = €350.

findings.claim: When a linked expense reaches endDate, processMonth writes a "Loan finished" row and zeroes the Loan balance whatever the rate type. For an interest-only loan, the notice it shows the same moment says the principal is still outstanding, and for variable-rate it says to check the balance with the lender. Savings vs. Owed then reports the debt as gone. No section of the spec asks for the balance to be zeroed at endDate.

Spec §9.1 (line 1052): "Its completion copy must not say \"paid off\" — the entire principal is still outstanding at that point."

findings.claim: Two paths set finishedAt, and only the month-boundary path emits §3.11's completion notice (and the linked-Loan closing row). advanceDueDates runs first on every open and sets finishedAt as soon as the last due date passes. So anyone who opens the app between the final occurrence and the next 1st never gets "Loan paid off" or the other notices. The test only passes because its fixture puts dueDate (15 Sep) past endDate (15 Aug), a state the real chain never reaches. Separately, for bimonthly/yearly, processMonth sweeps a share before it checks `first >= endDate`, so one share sweeps after endDate.
findings.evidence: Recurring.kt:161: `if (e.endDate != null && nxt > e.endDate) { finishedAt = finishedAt ?: today; break }`. NewMonth.kt:70: `if (e.endDate != null && e.finishedAt == null && first >= e.endDate) {` (runs after sweepOccurrences at line 66). Spec line 531: "On finishing, a plain, non-graded notice — \"Loan paid off — this Recurring Expense has ended\"". Test fixture: `dueDate = LocalDate(2026, 9, day)` with `endDate = LocalDate(2026, 8, 15)`.
findings.proposed_fix: Make one place own finishing. Either advanceDueDates records the Ended notice and pending state, or it leaves finishedAt to processMonth. For apportioned cadences, check endDate before sweeping (or cap sweepAmountForMonth at endDate). Add a test that walks the real chain: last due date, then an open the next day, then the 1st.

findings.claim: The auto-deposit switch only flips incomeAutoDeposit and never resets lastIncomeDepositDate. Suppose someone turns auto-deposit off for months, keeps Income on, and later turns it back on: the next open replays every payday since the old marker as real, dated deposits. This is the invented-money failure §3.3/§12 were amended to prevent.
findings.evidence: SettingsScreens.kt:245: `Switch(s.incomeAutoDeposit) { store.updateSettings { it.copy(incomeAutoDeposit = !it.incomeAutoDeposit) } }`. Income.kt:85: `val from = st.lastIncomeDepositDate?.plusDays(1) ?: st.incomePayDate ?: clock.today()`. Spec §12 (line 1294): "It starts `null` when auto-deposit is switched on, so the first deposit is the `incomePayDate` just supplied."
findings.proposed_fix: Route the toggle through an engine function (e.g. Income.setAutoDeposit) that sets lastIncomeDepositDate = null when it turns on. Add a test: off for 3 months with Income on, back on, and zero backfilled deposits.

findings.claim: A cadence change nulls incomePayDate (and incomePayDate2 when entering semimonthly), but nothing asks the question again. findings.evidence: Income.kt:150: `incomePayDate = null,`. SettingsScreens.kt:238: `DateField(s.incomePayDate ?: store.clock.today()) { ... }`. Spec §3.3 (line 373): "When `incomeCadence` changes, the app asks the plain fact question again for the new cadence — twice for semimonthly, once otherwise".
findings.proposed_fix: Either store the displayed default at the moment of the cadence change (today, editable), or render the field visibly empty with the question until it is answered. Add a test that a cadence change followed by no edit still yields a non-null anchor, or a visible unanswered state.

findings.claim: Deleting an Account that has a linked expense removes the expense with no §3.11 reversal prompt. The sheet offers only Cancel/Delete, and deleteCascade drops the expense without calling reversalAmount. The docstring claims the reversal prompt "has already run in the same flow", but no such step exists on the Account side. Un-elapsed swept money for a credit fixed payment or a loan payment is silently kept out of Savings.

findings.claim: catchUpSummaryPending is stored, but the card renders only from the in-memory state.catchUp of the open that ran the catch-up. After a restart in the same month, the pending flag is true and the card never shows. The GoalPrompt condition `!s.catchUpSummaryPending` then also hides §11.3's prompt, so an invisible state blocks it. The next month's open sets the flag back to false (`months.size > 1`) without anyone dismissing it. The stored accumulators catchUpDepositCount/Total that could rebuild the card are written and never read.
findings.evidence: BudgetScreen.kt:194: `val s = state.catchUp ?: return`. BudgetScreen.kt:235: `... && state.catchUp == null && !s.catchUpSummaryPending && ...`. NewMonth.kt:133: `catchUpSummaryPending = months.size > 1`. Spec line 468: "It persists until dismissed, tracked by `catchUpSummaryPending`". grep: catchUpDepositCount appears only in Income.kt:96 and Entities.kt:197.

findings.claim: Each point of the Age of Money trend is computed as of today's day-of-month in earlier months, not as of each month's final instant. §5.1 calls that rule load-bearing and warns that the anchor day alone changes the value (0, 12 or 28 days from identical data). savingsVsOwedTrend in the same file does use month-end.
findings.evidence: Reports.kt:55: `(months - 1 downTo 0).map { i -> val p = today.plusMonthsClamped(-i); MonthPoint(p, ageOfMoney(d, p).toLong()) }`. Spec line 791: "each computed by replaying the same FIFO walk as of the final instant of that calendar month, with the current month's point being the live value".
findings.proposed_fix: Use `p.firstOfNextMonth().minusDays(1)` for i > 0 and `today` for i = 0, matching savingsVsOwedTrend. Re-baseline the parity fixture if the prototype uses the same-day reading (and note that as prototype drift).

findings.claim: Loan auto-update decrement rows are dated to the 1st of the month with a fixed payee. §7.2 says they are dated to the sweep's real occurrence date, with the payee defaulting to the linked expense's name. findings.claim: The editor re-derives `months` from targetDate, floors it at 1, and on Save rewrites targetDate as today + months. Any save of a by-date goal (a rename, an icon change) whose deadline has passed moves the deadline to next month. Every save also re-anchors the day to today's. So the stored deadline decays through the editor, the failure §12 added targetDate to prevent.
findings.evidence: GoalEditing.kt:63: `val targetDate = ... draft.months?.let { today.plusMonthsClamped(it) }`. Goals.kt:42: `maxOf(1, (target.year - today.year) * 12 + ...)`. Spec line 875: "A Goal whose target date has passed while `saved < target` keeps counting."
findings.proposed_fix: Keep the stored targetDate unless the person changed the months or date field in the draft (track a dirty flag or keep targetDate in GoalDraft).

verdicts.reason: Reports.kt:38-47 reproduced: `var toConsume = -effect` and the loop `if (toConsume <= 0) break`. Whatever is left in toConsume is thrown away, no deficit is carried, and lines 49-50 return `oldest.first.daysTo(asOf)` without checking Savings <= 0. Spec §5.1 line 785 says the excess "is carried as a deficit that the next deposit absorbs" and "The figure floors at 0 when Savings ≤ 0". The only guard in BufferReport (ReportsScreen.kt:143) is `d.savings.amount == null`. ReportsTest.kt:36-47 has no deficit or overshoot case (grep for deficit/overshoot in the tests finds nothing). One caveat: the prototype's computeAgeOfMoney (sci-fin-prototype.html:1668-1692) has the same drop, and the parity fixture (ReportsTest.kt:111) compares native against it. So native matches the second oracle and diverges only from the authority, and the fixture may need re-baselining. Re-judged as decision because the Buffer figure the user sees changes and the two oracles disagree.

NewMonth.kt:76-80 reproduced: `if (acct.balance != 0L) { next = Ledger.logAndMove(... "Loan finished", date = first)` followed by `it.copy(balance = 0)`, with no check on rate type. completionNoticeFor (NewMonth.kt:37-45) returns the interest-only line "The principal is still outstanding." and the variable-rate line "Check the balance with your lender." in the same pass, so the notice contradicts the write. Spec §9.1 line 1052 says the interest-only principal is "still outstanding". A grep of the spec for a closing row, 'Loan finished' or zeroing finds no rule that zeroes a Loan at endDate. The only closing row in the §12 list (line 1293) is Account deletion. NewMonthTest.kt:74-85 asserts the zeroing, but only for a FIXED loan. Mitigating: because of the enddate-notice finding, this path is rarely reached in the real chain.

Recurring.kt:161 sets `finishedAt = finishedAt ?: today` when the next occurrence would pass endDate. NewMonth.runCatchUp (NewMonth.kt:118) calls Recurring.advanceDueDates BEFORE processMonth, and processMonth's notice branch (line 70) requires `e.finishedAt == null`. The defect is worse than the reviewer says: even on the 1st itself, runCatchUp's own advanceDueDates call sets finishedAt first (cur = last due date < today, next occurrence > endDate), so the notice and the Loan closing row never fire in the real chain, whatever the open timing. The test fixture helper (NewMonthTest.kt:24-26) gives `dueDate = LocalDate(2026, 9, day)`, and the test at lines 74-76 uses `endDate = LocalDate(2026, 8, 15)`, which is an unreachable state (dueDate past endDate). That is what lets advanceDueDates leave finishedAt null. Spec §3.11 line 531 requires the notice on the catch-up card. The secondary claim about apportioned cadences sweeping before the endDate check is consistent with line 66 running before line 70, but I did not trace sweepAmountForMonth end-to-end. Re-judged as decision because the fix changes which notices users see.

SettingsScreens.kt:245 reproduced: the Switch goes through the generic `store.updateSettings { it.copy(incomeAutoDeposit = !it.incomeAutoDeposit) }` (AppStore.kt:409), which has no clearing logic. incomeAutoDeposit is written nowhere else except Income.setEnabled(false) (Income.kt:132). Income.runCatchUp (Income.kt:85) resumes from `st.lastIncomeDepositDate?.plusDays(1)`, so a stale marker left from an earlier on-period replays every payday since then as a real dated deposit (loop at lines 84-91). Spec §3.3 line 381: "When auto-deposit is next switched on, `lastIncomeDepositDate` starts null". The §12 line 1294 wording is also reproduced. No test covers toggling auto-deposit alone. Re-judged as decision because it changes Savings figures the user sees, although the spec already settles the behaviour.

Income.kt:150 has `incomePayDate = null,` inside setCadence. SettingsScreens.kt:238 renders `DateField(s.incomePayDate ?: store.clock.today())`, so a null anchor is displayed as today. nextOccurrence (Income.kt:34) returns null without an anchor, so runCatchUp breaks at line 86 (`?: break`) and noIncomeLoggedDays returns null for MONTHLY (line 118) and SEMIMONTHLY (via mostRecentlyPassedAnchor, line 63). No code path re-asks the question: a grep for incomePayDate null-handling in commonMain finds only these sites. Spec §3.3 line 373: "the app asks the plain fact question again for the new cadence". The weekly and biweekly note paths use a threshold and are unaffected, which matches the reviewer's scoping.

Recurring.kt:244-247: applyReconcile logs only the `rec:` row (`TransactionKey.RecurringKey(e.id) ... RECONCILE_PAYEE`). Its only caller, AppStore.resolveReconcile (AppStore.kt:320-329), additionally changes just `interestRate` on the linked account (line 324). Nothing adjusts Account.balance or logs an `acct:` row. Spec §3.11 line 552: "a confirmed difference also adjusts `Account.balance` by the same amount as principal, and logs its own `acct:` Transaction".

ActivityScreens.kt:318-334: DeleteAccountSheet offers only Cancel and `Button("Delete", ...) { store.deleteAccount(a.id) }`, with no reversal step. AppStore.deleteAccount (358-362) calls Accounts.deleteCascade directly. deleteCascade (Accounts.kt:193-199) filters out the linked expense and never calls reversalAmount. Its KDoc at 190-192 claims "§3.11's reversal prompt has already run in the same flow where it applies", which is false. Spec §7.2 line 960: "§3.11's reversal prompt applies as normal, in the same flow."

Accounts.kt:175-181: retype to CREDIT clears autoUpdateFromPayments, principal, interestRate, termMonths, rateType and originationDate, but leaves linkedRecurringExpenseId untouched. The editor (ActivityScreens.kt:281) calls Accounts.retype inline. AccountEditing.save (AccountEditing.kt:15-35) has no retype or cascade branch and in fact re-links the expense (lines 32-34). Spec §7.2 line 963 requires that retyping "triggers the cascade prompt above for any linked Recurring Expense". The consequence 'goes on sweeping Savings' follows, since the linked expense is untouched.

BudgetScreen.kt:194: `val s = state.catchUp ?: return`. state.catchUp is set only from `opened.catchUp` at AppStore.kt:117, which is null on any open where NewMonth.runCatchUp takes the early return at NewMonth.kt:120-124, as on a restart in the same month. The persisted flag therefore survives while the card cannot render. BudgetScreen.kt:235's GoalPrompt condition includes `!s.catchUpSummaryPending`, so the invisible flag suppresses §11.3's prompt. NewMonth.kt:133 overwrites the flag with `months.size > 1`, so the next single-month boundary clears it undismissed. catchUpDepositCount and catchUpDepositTotal are read only in IncomeTest.kt:80 (a test), not in production code. Spec §3.9 line 468: "It persists until dismissed, tracked by `catchUpSummaryPending`". Re-judged as decision because it changes what card and prompt the user sees.

Reports.kt:54-55 reproduced: `val p = today.plusMonthsClamped(-i); MonthPoint(p, ageOfMoney(d, p)...)`, which gives the same day-of-month in earlier months. savingsVsOwedTrend in the same file (lines 117-120) uses `p.firstOfNextMonth().minusDays(1)`. The fix therefore needs the fixture re-baselined, and the two oracles disagree. Re-judged as decision because the chart the user sees changes.
